question: The internal bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R of ΔPQR meet at S. If m∠P = 75º, then m∠QSR is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When **internal bisectors** of two angles of a **triangle** meet at a point **S** (Incenter), the angle **∠QSR** is given by:

**∠QSR = 90º + (∠P ÷ 2)**

⇒ ∠QSR = 90º + (75º ÷ 2)

⇒ ∠QSR = 90º + 37.5º

⇒ ∠QSR = 127.5º

**∴ The correct answer is 127.5º.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In **ΔPQR**, m∠P = 75º. **QS** and **RS** are **angle bisectors** of ∠Q and ∠R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66354cb4032b86a90c532c554616574088198dc5e516ec4660922ee02a48816a.png] 

**Formula:** Sum of all internal angles of a triangle is 180º.

⇒ In **ΔPQR**: ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R = 180º

⇒ 75º + ∠Q + ∠R = 180º

⇒ ∠Q + ∠R = 180º − 75º = 105º

Since **QS** and **RS** are bisectors:

⇒ ∠SQR + ∠SRQ = (∠Q + ∠R) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠SQR + ∠SRQ = 105º ÷ 2 = 52.5º

In **ΔSQR**:

⇒ ∠QSR + ∠SQR + ∠SRQ = 180º

⇒ ∠QSR + 52.5º = 180º

⇒ ∠QSR = 180º − 52.5º = 127.5º

This result confirms that the required angle is 127.5º, matching **option (4)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 127.5º.**

**__Additional Information__**

Incenter of a Triangle

The **Incenter** (S) is the point where all three **internal angle bisectors** of a triangle intersect. It is the center of the **incircle**.

Ex-center Angle Formula

The angle formed by **external bisectors** of ∠Q and ∠R at point T is given by: **∠QTR = 90º − (∠P ÷ 2)**.

Incircle Radius (Inradius)

The **inradius** (r) can be calculated using the formula **r = Area ÷ semi-perimeter (s)**.</p
